newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Top Mauritius conglomerate IBL profits down 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Top Mauritius conglomerate IBL profits down 40 pct.

text.p: Profits of Ireland Blyth Ltd (IBL), the second largest conglomerate in Mauritius, fell 40 percent in the six months to June 30, 1996 to 25.44 million rupees ($1.26 million) compared to the same period in 1995.
IBL's turnover for the half year period edged up by three percent to 1.50 billion rupees from 1.45 billion rupees in 1995, the company said in a statement published on Thursday.
The IBL operating profit for the six months slumped by 67.1 percent to 4.87 million rupees and profit attributable to shareholders was down by 43.6 percent to 20.45 million rupees.
IBL blamed the slump in profit on difficult conditions prevailing in the commercial sector.

"However, as previously stated, the local commercial activities continue to be difficult and in the circumstances, this year's results are expected to approximate those of last year," the company said.

IBL reported pre-tax profit of 50.3 million rupees for the whole year 1995, turnover of 2.85 billion rupees, operating profit of 165,000 rupees and profit attributable to shareholders of 32.1 million rupees.
The company said some of the conglomerate's associated companies also posted worse financial results but forecast better results for the conglomerate in the longer run.

"The board is of opinion that the recent cost-cutting exercise, the restructuring of activities and a number of projects currently under study will generate the anticipated turnaround in profitability over the medium term," it said.
